destination.title: Conditional consistency tests and observational inference
destination.question: Which inflationary models or trajectories satisfy the particular conjectural inequalities being tested, and which observational conclusions follow under the required assumptions?
destination.summary: Keeps conjecture choice, numerical constants, perturbation source, normalization and tested domain explicit.

systems: Source-specific inflationary models and scalar potentials
targets: Compatibility tests and the validity of exclusion arguments
regimes: Selected inflationary intervals versus entire relevant positive-potential domains
assumptions: Original gradient criteria and refined disjunctions are different tests
A printed TCC energy ceiling is not automatically a duration-dependent TCC check
conventions: Use the appropriate scalar metric and canonical normalization
Positive potential curvature does not satisfy a negative-Hessian branch
includes: Distance, gradient, curvature, entropy and scalar-interaction tests when explicitly specified
excludes: Current observational fits inferred from dated comparisons

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can observations exclude inflation through proposed field-range and potential-slope criteria without establishing the source of the final curvature perturbation or the numerical strength of the slope criterion?

sources.title: Note on single-field inflation and the swampland criteria

evidence.text: Can single-field inflation satisfy conjectural quantum-gravity restrictions on its potential while reproducing a small tensor-to-scalar ratio and a nearly scale-invariant scalar spectrum?

sources.title: Spinodal solution to swampland inflationary constraints

evidence.text: Does a potential-slope restriction exclude inflation when non-equilibrium fluctuations control the evolution? The authors propose assessing the relevant slope safety through the potential-driven stage.

sources.title: Relating the scalar weak gravity conjecture and the swampland distance conjecture for an accelerating universe

evidence.text: How strongly do the original and revised scalar interaction inequalities constrain positive potentials approaching an inflationary plateau?

sources.title: Swampland, axions, and minimal warm inflation

evidence.text: Which conjectural restrictions on scalar potentials, field-space excursion, and primordial fluctuation histories are imposed on the inflationary examples?

sources.title: Warm tachyon inflation and swampland criteria

evidence.text: Test selected trajectories against conjectural excursion and slope inequalities, while distinguishing the tachyon coordinate from the canonically normalized scalar in the reviewed cold-inflation comparison.

sources.title: Reconstructing $k$-essence: Unifying the attractor $n_S(N)$ and the swampland criteria

evidence.text: Test whether the reconstructed inflationary functions satisfy conjectural restrictions on scalar displacement and potential steepness. The source applies these inequalities directly to φ despite its field-dependent kinetic coefficient.

sources.title: Revisiting Scalar Tensor inflation by swampland criteria and Reheating

evidence.text: Do the observationally selected inflationary examples also obey the paper's conjectural limits on field excursion and potential slope? These cuts are applied as additional conditions on model parameters.

sources.title: Rejuvenating the hope of a swampland consistent inflated multiverse with tachyonic inflation in the high-energy RS-II braneworld

evidence.text: The reviewed problem is whether inflation can simultaneously produce sufficient expansion and acceptable perturbations while obeying conjectural limits on scalar displacement, potential derivatives and horizon-entropy loss.

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland Conjecture on Inflation in General Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: The framework asks how restrictions motivated by quantum gravity constrain scalar potentials used for cosmological inflation.

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland Conjecture on Inflation in General Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: Can a parameter triple that works at one inflationary point satisfy the same conjecture throughout the displayed potential's positive domain?

sources.title: Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture in Super Yang-Mills Inflationary Model

evidence.text: Can any inflationary potential satisfy all considered conjectural constraints across its full relevant domain, rather than only on selected intervals?

sources.title: Primordial Gravitational Waves and the Swampland

evidence.text: Determine whether quantum-gravity conjectures can restrict primordial tensor amplitudes without excluding canonical single-field slow-roll inflation with roughly 60 e-folds. The paper focuses on how uncertain conjecture parameters affect this compatibility.

sources.title: Higgs inflation and scalar weak gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can metric Higgs inflation, Higgs–Dilaton inflation, or Palatini Higgs inflation satisfy the further-refining de Sitter swampland conjecture together with both SWGC and its strong version?

sources.title: Starobinsky inflation and swampland conjectures

evidence.text: Does Starobinsky inflation conflict with the simplest versions of three swampland conjectures: no global symmetries, weak gravity, and no de Sitter or eternal inflation?

sources.title: Inflation models selected by the swampland distance conjecture with the Lyth bound

evidence.text: Can the swampland distance conjecture, combined with the Lyth bound and model-specific predictions, restrict representative large-field inflation models more strongly than the paper's quoted CMB constraints?

sources.title: Higher Curvature Inflation and the Species Scale

evidence.text: Can an infinite series of higher curvature corrections and a field-dependent species cutoff compensate their exponential field dependence, producing inflationary plateaus compatible with the Swampland Distance Conjecture?

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Let a light spectator field shift the inflaton value at which inflation ends. Convert the induced shift of the end surface into a perturbation of local inflationary duration and hence into curvature.

sources.title: Primordial Gravitational Waves and the Swampland

evidence.text: Integrate the canonical field speed in e-fold time, and use a lower bound on that speed to constrain the total excursion. In this paper, the operation converts a conjectural EFT field-range cap into a tensor upper bound.

sources.title: Note on single-field inflation and the swampland criteria

evidence.text: Compute Q and the potential and dissipation derivatives, test the warm slow-roll hierarchy, and solve the friction balance when acceleration is negligible. Bath stability and perturbations require separate checks.

sources.title: Spinodal solution to swampland inflationary constraints

evidence.text: Expand in fluctuations, apply a monomial closure, resum, and evolve the quadratic modes with their self-consistent variance. For natural inflation, the presented output suppresses the periodic force and curvature while preserving the constant Λ⁴ energy contribution.

sources.title: Relating the scalar weak gravity conjecture and the swampland distance conjecture for an accelerating universe

evidence.text: Differentiate the assumed potential, evaluate the chosen diagnostic, and retain curvature signs and singularities. The logarithmic recurrence reconstructs the paper's operation without adopting the suspect fourth-derivative expression.

sources.title: Swampland, axions, and minimal warm inflation

evidence.text: Map a potential and bath parameters to a trajectory, select a consistent endpoint, integrate the desired duration, evaluate observables, and compare the reduced solution with full background evolution.

sources.title: Non-canonical kinetic structures in the swampland

evidence.text: DBI supplies a motivated example in which a relativistic speed limit permits inflation on potentials too steep for canonical slow roll. The paper tests the associated potential-gradient estimate.

sources.title: Chaotic inflation on the brane and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Can modified expansion in a braneworld support single-field slow-roll inflation with a small field excursion and an order-one potential slope while retaining acceptable scalar and tensor spectra?

sources.title: Rapid-Turn Inflationary Attractors

evidence.text: Can rapid-turn inflation satisfy a conjectural small-excursion requirement together with either a steep potential or a sufficiently negative Hessian eigenvalue?

sources.title: Modular Inflation at Higher Level $N$

evidence.text: Can a positive covariant-gradient lower bound coexist with slow-roll modular inflation and its tensor predictions?

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can altered degrees of freedom, kinetic terms, initial states, or conjectural criteria evade the conventional scalar-power argument?

sources.title: The Convex Hull Swampland Distance Conjecture and Bounds on Non-geodesics

evidence.text: Can integrating out heavy scalars change which trajectories are geodesic and thereby change whether a light-field EFT appears to satisfy the SDC?

sources.title: Chaotic inflation on the brane and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: Which changes to the perturbation source, inflationary dynamics, or initial state have been proposed to ease the conjectural constraints?

sources.title: Non-canonical kinetic structures in the swampland

evidence.text: Small ε describes quasi-de Sitter expansion, while small η permits persistent inflation. These conditions constrain the expansion history without requiring a shallow potential or automatically negligible scalar acceleration.

sources.title: The Convex Hull Swampland Distance Conjecture and Bounds on Non-geodesics

evidence.text: Does one scalar measure of bending characterize SDC-compatible trajectories when different hyperbolic factors and growth sectors are available?

sources.title: Primordial Gravitational Waves and the Swampland

evidence.text: The analyzed inflationary regime has one canonical light field and uses potential slow-roll parameters to relate quantum-gravity inequalities to tensor production. Monotonic growth of ε lets a lower instantaneous field speed constrain the total field excursion.

sources.title: Distance Conjecture and De-Sitter Quantum Gravity

evidence.text: Can a bound derived from static radial deformations inform inflationary slow-roll constraints? The paper leaves this open because it supplies no dictionary relating the radial profile to a time-dependent cosmological solution.

sources.title: The string swampland constraints require multi-field inflation

evidence.text: Do conjectured restrictions on field distance and potential steepness exclude inflation, or can a non-geodesic trajectory sustain slow expansion despite a steep total potential gradient?

sources.title: Further Refining Swampland Conjecture on Inflation in General Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity

evidence.text: Can E-model, T-model, and quantum-corrected scalar-tensor inflation satisfy conjectured restrictions on the slope and curvature of a positive scalar potential?

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Can a scalar drive inflation through a canonical field excursion exceeding the Planck scale while remaining in the string landscape? The paper proposes a negative answer and tests selected constructions.

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes and the String Swampland

evidence.text: The inflationary setting translates restrictions on a scalar potential into restrictions on primordial perturbations through canonical single-field slow-roll relations.

sources.title: Draining the Swampland

evidence.text: Can an additional scalar provide the gradient required by C1 without controlling symmetry breaking, inflationary observables or present acceleration?

sources.title: Hyperinflation generalised: from its attractor mechanism to its tension with the ‘swampland conditions’

evidence.text: Determine which geometric, potential and initial-condition assumptions are essential for rapid-turn inflation, and whether relaxing them permits models compatible with scalar observations and the particular quantum-gravity conjectures examined in the paper.

sources.title: Eternal Inflation, Entropy Bounds and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can stochastic uphill motion evade scalar-potential constraints without violating a horizon-entropy bound, and can a region leaving that regime subsequently produce sufficient expansion and acceptable cosmological perturbations?

sources.title: Swampland Constraints on No-Boundary Quantum Cosmology

evidence.text: How do finite plateau width and the characteristic field-range parameter α affect compatibility between no-boundary inflation and the conjectural gradient, curvature and distance limits?

sources.title: Reconstructing $k$-essence: Unifying the attractor $n_S(N)$ and the swampland criteria

evidence.text: Determine whether a scalar inflation model can reproduce a prescribed spectral-index attractor while obeying assumed bounds on field excursion and potential slope. The unknown functions are the potential and the coefficient of the scalar kinetic term.

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: How much scalar motion does tensor production require over an inflationary interval, and can that motion remain below an order-one distance bound?

sources.title: Avoiding the string swampland in single-field inflation: Excited initial states

evidence.text: Can additional gravitational friction permit inflation on a steep canonical scalar potential without weakening the conjectured slope bound?

sources.title: Eternal Inflation and Swampland Conjectures

evidence.text: Can self-reproducing inflation coexist with a finite effective-theory field range and a lower bound on the gradient of a positive scalar potential? The paper studies this compatibility conditionally, with explicit calculations for one slowly rolling inflaton.

sources.title: Gauss–Bonnet Inflation and the String Swampland

evidence.text: Can a scalar-dependent curvature coupling change inflationary observables enough to accommodate a steep potential and a small field excursion?
